svg.title: ISO 12100 risk assessment and the 3-step risk reduction loop
svg.text: ISO 12100 – risk assessment (steps 1–4) and iterative risk reduction (step 5, 3-step method)
For an FMS: done for the ASSEMBLY by its manufacturer (integrator or owner), in addition to each module's own assessment.

g.text: 1 Limits of the machine
use, space, time, persons, all life phases
2 Hazard identification
checklist (Annex B), tasks, zones, what-if at interfaces
3 Risk estimation
severity S, exposure F, avoidance P → PLr (risk graph)
4 Risk evaluation:
adequately reduced?
yes
Document – technical file
risk assessment, residual risks → instructions, DoC, CE
no
5 Risk reduction – strictly in this order
Step 1 Inherently safe design
lower speeds / forces, fail-safe clamp (holds without energy),
layout separating people and AGV routes, rounded edges,
load station outside the pool aisle, 24 V PELV controls
Step 2 Safeguarding + complementary measures
fences (ISO 13857), interlocked doors + guard locking (ISO 14119),
light curtains / scanners at distance S (ISO 13855),
safety functions with PL ≥ PLr (ISO 13849), e-stop (ISO 13850),
LOTO means, escape release
Step 3 Information for use
signs, lamps, instructions, training, PPE, maintenance (T10d,
proof tests) – never instead of a possible safeguard
After each measure: back to step 2 – did the measure create new hazards?

svg.text: Teaching diagram after ISO 12100; use the current edition and the C-standards (ISO 11161, ISO 16090-1, ISO 10218-2, ISO 3691-4, EN 528).
